AWS GLUE: Optimize your Jobs Spark and Reduce Costs (Practical Guide for Beginners)

Video is a guide for those who start on AWS Glue: When you choose Glue instead of Amazon EMR, how to configure the job (worker type and execution class), how to investigate performance in CloudWatch and Spark interface, and how to reduce shuffle with filters, cache, more features and Adaptive Query Execution.

Where Glue Fits

Video is a practical guide for those who start on AWS Glue and want jobs Spark efficient from day one 00:00.

For a quick ETL project, without managing a server, Glue is the choice. Amazon EMR is a Swiss penknife for big data: more powerful and flexible, but more work to set up 00:00. For starters, Glue is the simplest way 00:21.

The script: what is Glue, the configuration of the first job, performance research, optimizations and good practices 00:42.

AWS Glue is a fully managed and serverless data integration service. AWS handles the infrastructure, and the team focuses on preparing and combining data for analysis 01:04.

Configure the first job

The configuration has four steps 01:24:

1. Set general job properties 01:45. 2. Choose the type of worker 01:45. 3. Set job parameters 01:454. 4. Choose the execution class, which affects the start cost and time 01:45.

The most critical decision is the type of worker: it defines the performance and cost of the job, as the engine of a car 02:06.

The guys form a power ladder. G.1X serves for common transformations and consultations; G.2X is the medium-term, with good cost-benefit for most works 02:06. For complex aggregations and joins, it rises to the larger types, with more vCPUs and memory to process in parallel 02:29.

The execution class is the other decision 02:50:

  • Standard: Job starts fast, with dedicated features, for critical tasks 02:50.
  • Flex: the most economical option, for jobs without hurry, as a lot of dawn when the start time may vary 02:50.

Investigating performance

With the job running, the question is if it spins well 03:11. If you're slow or failing, where to start? 03:32

There are two panels. Amazon CloudWatch is the thermometer: gives the overview and shows if something is wrong 03:32. Spark's interface is the X-ray. 03:54.

In CloudWatch, the key metric is bytes written in shuffle. A high value indicates that the job spends a lot of time reorganizing data between the machines, an expensive operation that moves a lot of data over the network and appears in joins and groupings 03:54.

In the Spark interface, the Jobs tab shows each step. Look for steps that take too long or tasks that have failed: are suspicions of bottleneck 04:16.

The Executors tab shows the cluster processing power. The Colors column tells how many tasks run in parallel 04:37.

Optimize

The shuffle is almost always the villain of the Spark performance. It's like organizing a deck of millions of cards spread across multiple tables; minimizing shuffle is the secret 04:59.

The first strategy attacks the joins, one of the most common causes of shuffle 05:20:

  • Filter unnecessary rows and columns before join 05:20.
  • cache, memory, dataset used several times, for Spark not to recalculate 05:43.

The second strategy is to give the job more resources: increase the number of workers, choose a larger worker or, better, activate Auto Scaling, which adds and removes resources as needed 05:43.

The newest versions of Spark bring the Adaptive Query Execution (AQE), which optimizes the job while running and handles data unbalancing (data skew), when a worker gets overloaded and others wait 06:26.

Checklist

The Bottom Flow 06:48:

1. Configure: Choose the right worker for the load 06:48. 2. Monitor: CloudWatch for overview, Spark interface for diagnosis 06:48. 3. Identify the necks: slow steps and high shuffle 07:09. 4. Optimize: filter early, use cache and increase resources if needed 07:09. 5. Automate: use Auto Scaling and Adaptive Query Execution 07:09.

The final provocation: optimizing for today's data is one thing; and when the volume grows 100 times? Thinking of scale from the beginning is what differentiates a good job 07:09.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which setting weighs most on the cost of a Glue job?

The kind of worker. It defines the power of the job and thus the performance and cost 02:06.

How do you know shuffle is the problem?

In CloudWatch, by the byte metric written in the shuffle. If it's high, the job is moving a lot of data between the machines 03:54.

About the video

Stop spending money on slow jobs on AWS Glue! In this practical and direct guide to the point, you will learn step by step to optimize your Jobs Spark on AWS Glue, ensuring more performance and less costs in your data architecture.

If you are starting with AWS Glue and Apache Spark, or if your jobs are taking longer than they should, this video is for you! We unveil the Spark jobs optimization process in 5 simple steps, ideal for beginners who want to build efficient and scalable data pipelines.

What you'll learn:

1. Essential Settings: Understand the difference between AWS Glue and Amazon EMR and how the correct choice of Worker Type and Execution Class directly impacts your cost and performance.

2. Performance Monitoring: Learn how to use Apache Spark's AWS CloudWatch and UI to identify the true bottlenecks of your jobs, such as the dreaded data shuffle.

3. Optimization strategies: Discover advanced but easy-to-apply techniques, such as filtering data before joins, using cache intelligently and the importance of Spark's Adaptive Query Run.

4. Scaleability and Automation: Learn to scale your resources manually or via Auto Scaling to handle different volumes of data.

This video is perfect for:

• Beginner Data Engineers.

• Developers working with AWS Glue.

• Anyone who wants to reduce the AWS invoice by optimizing the use of Spark.

Don't waste time on inefficient jobs! Watch now and transform the performance of your data pipelines!
